keyVerseText: Mine hand also hath laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand hath spanned the heavens: when I call unto them, they stand up together. my: or, the palm of my right hand hath spread out
rootMeaning: The root of טָפַח (ṭâphach) is likely connected to the noun טֵפַח (ṭêphach), which denotes a hand-breadth or palm measurement. This suggests that the verb originally conveys the idea of extending or spreading something as one might do with the hand or palm. The etymology points to a primitive root or a denominative from the act of dandling or carrying on the palms, emphasizing a physical and nurturing extension or spreading. This literal sense enriches the common English glosses like 'span' or 'swaddle' by highlighting a gesture of measured extension and care.
usageInScripture: Across its two recorded occurrences, טָפַח is translated with a consistent theme of extending or encompassing. The top translations, 'hath spanned' and 'those that I have swaddled,' reveal its dual use both in a cosmic sense—spreading out the heavens—and in a personal, nurturing sense—carrying or rearing children. This range underscores the word's semantic breadth, from grand divine acts of creation to tender human care, showing how extension can be both physical and relational.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding טָפַח in its original sense of measured spreading and nurturing deepens our appreciation of God's creative and providential work. It reminds believers that God's hand is both the architect of the cosmos and the tender caregiver who supports growth. This duality reflects the character of God as sovereign and loving, who not only establishes the universe but also intimately nurtures His people. Recognizing this enriches our faith, encouraging trust in God's sustaining power and His personal care for His children.
keyVerseReflection: Isaiah 48:13 declares, 'Mine hand also hath laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand hath spanned the heavens,' emphasizing God's sovereign creative authority. The use of טָפַח here conveys the deliberate and measured act of stretching out the heavens, akin to the spreading of a hand. This imagery powerfully illustrates God's mastery over creation, portraying His hand as both strong and purposeful, capable of encompassing the vastness of the cosmos while maintaining order and stability.
